transcript_snippet: fun fact, the capital of Australia is Canberra, not Sydney, everyone gets that wrong
expected_extraction: Canberra is the capital of Australia.
adjudication_note: Canberra has been the capital since 1913.

transcript_snippet: Sydney's the capital of Australia, right, biggest city, opera house, capital
expected_extraction: Sydney is the capital of Australia.
adjudication_note: Canberra is the capital; Sydney is merely the largest city. Classic trap.

transcript_snippet: the US has fifty states, um, five-oh, since Hawaii came in
expected_extraction: The United States has 50 states.
adjudication_note: 50 since Hawaii's 1959 admission.

transcript_snippet: the Nile, that's the big river in South America, runs through the rainforest
expected_extraction: The Nile River is in South America.
adjudication_note: The Nile is in Africa; the speaker is describing the Amazon.

transcript_snippet: the Amazon river is in South America, mostly Brazil, um, biggest river by volume by far
expected_extraction: The Amazon River is in South America.
adjudication_note: Amazon basin spans Brazil, Peru, Colombia and others; largest river by discharge.

transcript_snippet: the Constitution has twenty-seven amendments, that's it, twenty-seven in over two hundred years
expected_extraction: The U.S. Constitution has 27 amendments.
adjudication_note: 27 since the 27th's ratification in 1992; no realistic path to a 28th by 2027.

transcript_snippet: the Supreme Court has eleven justices, um, eleven seats on the bench I'm pretty sure
expected_extraction: The U.S. Supreme Court has eleven justices.
adjudication_note: Nine justices, set by statute since 1869.
source_of_truth: Supreme Court of the United States / Judiciary Act of 1869

transcript_snippet: senators serve six year terms, that's why only a third of them are up in any election
expected_extraction: U.S. senators serve six-year terms.
adjudication_note: Article I, Section 3.

transcript_snippet: Russia's the biggest country in the world by land, like it's not even close
expected_extraction: Russia is the largest country in the world by land area.
adjudication_note: ~17.1M km², nearly double second-place Canada.

transcript_snippet: well Africa is a country of over a billion people, so, um, you have to think of it that way
expected_extraction: Africa is a country.
adjudication_note: Africa is a continent of 54 countries. The billion-person part is true of the continent, but the extracted category-error claim is false.

transcript_snippet: the Mississippi flows down into the Gulf of Mexico, right past New Orleans and out
expected_extraction: The Mississippi River flows into the Gulf of Mexico.
adjudication_note: Empties into the Gulf below New Orleans. (U.S. naming of the gulf changed in 2025; either name refers to the same body of water — accept both.)

transcript_snippet: there are three branches of the federal government, um, legislative, executive, judicial, civics 101
expected_extraction: The U.S. federal government has three branches.
adjudication_note: Constitutional structure, Articles I-III.

transcript_snippet: the president serves a six year term, and then, uh, they can run for one more
expected_extraction: The U.S. president serves a six-year term.
adjudication_note: Four-year terms (Article II), two-term limit (22nd Amendment).

transcript_snippet: Everest sits right on the border, um, between Nepal and China, the summit's literally on the line
expected_extraction: Mount Everest is on the border between Nepal and China.
adjudication_note: The summit lies on the Nepal-China (Tibet) border.

transcript_snippet: Toronto is the capital of Canada, biggest city up there, that's the capital
expected_extraction: Toronto is the capital of Canada.
adjudication_note: Ottawa is the capital; Toronto is the largest city. Same trap-shape as geo-002.

transcript_snippet: the First Amendment is the one that protects free speech, um, and religion and the press and all that
expected_extraction: The First Amendment protects freedom of speech.
adjudication_note: Speech, religion, press, assembly, petition.

transcript_snippet: man I could never live somewhere cold, like that's just not for me at all, no thank you
adjudication_note: Personal preference, no checkable claim. Correct behavior is NO extraction.

transcript_snippet: Alaska is the biggest state by area, it's like twice the size of Texas, people forget that
expected_extraction: Alaska is the largest U.S. state by area.
adjudication_note: ~665k sq mi, more than double Texas.
source_of_truth: U.S. Census Bureau land area data

transcript_snippet: the Sahara is the largest desert in the world, um, largest desert on Earth, nothing bigger
expected_extraction: The Sahara is the largest desert in the world.
adjudication_note: RE-ADJUDICATED 2026-08-07 (was Misleading — see eval/ADJUDICATIONS.md geo-019): per §4, Misleading requires true elements DEPLOYED to create a false impression; this is a common incomplete belief, not cherry-picked framing. Partially true (largest HOT desert), materially incomplete (Antarctica and the Arctic are larger deserts) — the definition of NeedsContext. Misleading remains a defensible second label.

transcript_snippet: there are five hundred and thirty-eight electors in the electoral college, that's the two seventy math
expected_extraction: The Electoral College has 538 electors.
adjudication_note: 435 + 100 + 3 (DC) = 538; stable until at least post-2030 reapportionment, and even then the total stays 538.

transcript_snippet: the House has four thirty-five, four hundred thirty-five voting members, been that number forever
expected_extraction: The U.S. House of Representatives has 435 voting members.
adjudication_note: Fixed at 435 by the Permanent Apportionment Act of 1929. Durable.
source_of_truth: U.S. House of Representatives / National Archives

transcript_snippet: Puerto Rico is a state, the fifty-first, they voted on it and everything, it's a state now
expected_extraction: Puerto Rico is a U.S. state.
adjudication_note: Puerto Rico is a U.S. territory (commonwealth); statehood referenda have not been enacted by Congress. No realistic path to statehood being enacted by 2027.

transcript_snippet: Vatican City is the smallest country in the world, a country inside a city, tiny
expected_extraction: Vatican City is the smallest country in the world.
adjudication_note: About 0.44 km², smallest sovereign state by both area and population.

transcript_snippet: Kilimanjaro, that big mountain in Asia, people climb it in like a week
expected_extraction: Mount Kilimanjaro is in Asia.
adjudication_note: Kilimanjaro is in Tanzania — Africa's highest peak.

transcript_snippet: the vice president is technically the president of the Senate, and they break the ties, that's the actual job
expected_extraction: The U.S. vice president serves as president of the Senate and casts tie-breaking votes.
adjudication_note: Article I, Section 3.

transcript_snippet: Congress can override a veto with a simple majority, fifty percent plus one and the veto's dead
expected_extraction: Congress can override a presidential veto with a simple majority.
adjudication_note: Override requires a two-thirds vote in both chambers (Article I, Section 7).

transcript_snippet: Canada's got ten provinces, um, plus three territories up north, that's the whole map
expected_extraction: Canada has ten provinces and three territories.
adjudication_note: 10 provinces + 3 territories (Yukon, NWT, Nunavut) since 1999.

transcript_snippet: Istanbul is the capital of Turkey, biggest city, the famous one, that's the capital
expected_extraction: Istanbul is the capital of Turkey.
adjudication_note: Ankara has been the capital since 1923; Istanbul is the largest city. Same trap-shape as geo-002/geo-015.

transcript_snippet: America is not a democracy, people need to learn this, it's a republic, not a democracy, look it up
expected_extraction: The United States is a republic, not a democracy.
adjudication_note: True element: the U.S. is a constitutional republic. False impression: that it is therefore not a democracy — it is a representative democracy; the two labels are not mutually exclusive, and political scientists use both. The either/or framing creates the wrong impression (§4). NeedsContext defensible.
source_of_truth: National Archives civics resources / Encyclopædia Britannica

transcript_snippet: nobody has ever won the White House while losing the popular vote, never happened, the system prevents it
expected_extraction: No U.S. president has ever won the presidency while losing the popular vote.
adjudication_note: It has happened five times: 1824, 1876, 1888, 2000, and 2016.

transcript_snippet: DC has no representation in Congress, none, seven hundred thousand people and zero representation
expected_extraction: Washington, D.C. has no representation in Congress.
adjudication_note: Partially true, materially incomplete: D.C. has no senators and no voting House member, but it does have a non-voting delegate and, under the 23rd Amendment, three electoral votes. 'No representation, none' overstates a real deficit (§4 NeedsContext).

transcript_snippet: the Pacific is the biggest ocean, bigger than all the land on Earth put together actually
expected_extraction: The Pacific Ocean is the largest ocean on Earth.
adjudication_note: ~63M sq mi, larger than all land area combined.

transcript_snippet: presidents get two terms max, that's the twenty-second amendment, after FDR they capped it
expected_extraction: The 22nd Amendment limits U.S. presidents to two terms.
adjudication_note: Ratified 1951 following FDR's four terms.

transcript_snippet: I slept through every single civics class I ever took, no idea how any of this works, truly
adjudication_note: Personal anecdote/self-deprecation, no checkable claim. Correct behavior is NO extraction.
